Case 01 · Real Estate

Shang Properties

Creative test → lead → confirmed closed deal

Business outcome over vanity metrics.

The campaign was generating leads, but CPL was higher than an external benchmark being referenced. Instead of abandoning the existing structure, I continued testing new creatives and evaluated acquisition efficiency alongside downstream lead quality.

3Leads
₱90.15CPL
2.69%Link CTR
Outcome: the client confirmed that one of the leads generated by the newly introduced “Getting a Shang Home” creative became a closed property deal.

Case 02 · Local Service

Rob Peralta

Knowing when NOT to kill an ad

I sourced an organic video from the client's Facebook Page and tested it alongside agency-produced creatives. On day one it generated 2 conversations at ₱94.96 CPR. Rather than judge an immature sample, I monitored it as spend and conversions accumulated.

₱94.96Day-1 CPR
₱29.28Later CPR
190Conversations
The decision was not prematurely killing a potentially strong creative before it had enough data.

When lead quality was questioned, I also reviewed Page inbox conversations and provided recommendations around prospect handling and service positioning.

Case 04 · Automotive

V-car

Controlled copy testing

I selected a proven video, kept the asset unchanged, and tested different ad copy—isolating messaging as the main variable.

About

I don't optimize from one metric.

A high CPM doesn't automatically mean an ad is failing. A high CTR doesn't automatically mean an ad is winning. And a cheap lead doesn't automatically mean a quality lead.

I look at delivery, creative response, conversion efficiency and downstream lead quality together before deciding whether to scale, fix or stop.
